findings.summary: Christopher Buskirk (b. ~1968-69, US military base in Germany, raised Scottsdale AZ). BA Political Science, Claremont McKenna College. Publius Fellow at Claremont Institute, Earhart Foundation fellowship. Serial entrepreneur in financial services (Buskirk Capital — insurance, reinsurance, specialty lending, tax-credit financing). Sold businesses ~2015. Founded American Greatness blog 2016. Publisher/editor American Greatness, co-author of 'American Greatness' book (2017). Co-founded Rockbridge Network 2019 with JD Vance. Co-founded 1789 Capital (Oct 2022) with Omeed Malik and Rebekah Mercer, serving as Founder & CIO. President of Faithful in Action (160K+ members, Christian voter mobilization). Founder of Turnout for America super PAC ($45.67M raised). Position at PublicSq (PSQ Holdings, via Colombier SPAC merger). Confidant of Peter Thiel, friends with RFK Jr and JD Vance. LittleSis entity 439747. FEC donations: Blake Masters, WinRed, Ohioans for JD, America 21 PAC.

Buskirk personal FEC donations totaling ~K+ in 2024 cycle: K to Trump 47 Committee, .7K to RNC, K to Save America, .6K to Never Surrender Inc, K to Vance Victory, .8K to Blake Masters for Congress, .3K to WinRed. Employer listed as 'self-employed' or 'CAG' or 'American Greatness'. Located in Paradise Valley, AZ.

findings.summary: Buskirk co-founded Rockbridge Network with JD Vance in 2019. Rockbridge steers 8 organizations: 4 non-disclosing 501(c)(4)s, 2 super PACs, 1 donor-advised 501(c)(3), and the umbrella LLC. ~$75M budget for 2024 cycle. Donors include Peter Thiel, Rebekah Mercer, Cameron/Tyler Winklevoss. ~150-200 members paying $100K-$1M dues. Firebrand Action (501c4, est. 2022) handles Rockbridge efforts on journalism. Turnout for America is one of Rockbridge's two super PACs.

Buskirk is co-owner of Executive Branch, ultra-exclusive MAGA private club in Georgetown DC, alongside Donald Trump Jr., Omeed Malik, Alex Witkoff and Zach Witkoff (sons of Steve Witkoff, Trump Middle East envoy). Founding membership fee: $500K. Founding members include David Sacks, Chamath Palihapitiya, Winklevoss twins, Jeff Miller. Attendees include Sec. Rubio, AG Bondi, DNI Gabbard, FCC chair Carr, FTC chair Ferguson, SEC chair Atkins, Dan Bongino, Mehmet Oz. Club is designed to allow business executives private access to Trump advisors and Cabinet members.

Buskirk is Founder and CIO of 1789 Capital, anti-ESG venture capital firm co-founded with Omeed Malik (Founder/President) and Rebekah Mercer in Oct 2022. The fund has topped $1B in assets, investing in SpaceX, xAI, and Neuralink. Donald Trump Jr. joined the firm. 1789 Capital emerged from the Rockbridge Network.

America 21 PAC (C00804690) is a super PAC registered Feb 2022, closely linked to Buskirk. He donated $30,500 personally. PAC received $800K from Saving Arizona PAC (Peter Thiel-funded Blake Masters vehicle), $750K from Turnout for America, $87.6K from Michigan Strong. Uses identical vendor network as TFA: Telperion LLC, Timoleon LLC, Pulse Associates, Crosby Ottenhoff, Holtzman Vogel, Howard Sckolnik CPA, Chain Bridge Bank. Largest disbursement: $750K to MAGA KY (anti-Thomas Massie PAC run by Republican strategists Fabrizio/LaCivita). Paul Singer donated $1M in Nov 2025. Total receipts across 3 cycles: $3.64M.

Turnout for America and America 21 PAC share identical vendor infrastructure: Telperion LLC (Wilmington, DE) for management consulting/rent, Timoleon LLC (political strategy), Pulse Associates LLC (research/media/donor development), Crosby Ottenhoff Group (compliance), Holtzman Vogel PLLC (legal), Howard Sckolnik CPA (accounting), and Chain Bridge Bank (banking). Both also receive monthly interest deposits from Chain Bridge Bank. This shared vendor network strongly suggests common operational control by Buskirk.

evidence.evidence_ref: FEC Schedule B filings for C00883520 and C00804690

findings.summary: Chain Bridge Bank (McLean, VA), founded by ex-Sen. Peter Fitzgerald, is the banking institution for both Turnout for America and America 21 PAC. Known as 'the bank of the Republican Party,' it has served every GOP presidential campaign since McCain 2008 and the RNC since 2008. The bank makes monthly interest deposits to both PACs: ~$28-39K/month to TFA and ~$1.9-4.5K/month to America 21. Chain Bridge had its IPO in Oct 2024, raising $41M, with its fortunes explicitly tied to the Republican Party's success.

Buskirk 2021-2022 cycle FEC donations: $30,500 to America 21 PAC, $5,800 to Ohioans for JD (Vance super PAC), $2,900 to JD Vance for Senate, $2,900 to Working for Ohio, $5,800 to WinRed. All donations listed employer as 'CAG' (Center for American Greatness). His son Christopher Buskirk Jr. (student, Paradise Valley AZ) donated $500 to Brandon Gill for Texas in Jan 2024.

curation.lead:
Chris Buskirk (born ~1968-69, Claremont McKenna College graduate) is a Scottsdale-based political entrepreneur who co-founded the Rockbridge Network with JD Vance in 2019, co-founded 1789 Capital with Omeed Malik and Rebekah Mercer in October 2022, and publishes the conservative media outlet American Greatness [Finding #6735]. Before entering political media, Buskirk spent two decades in financial services — insurance, reinsurance, specialty lending, and tax-credit financing — through entities including JAS Intermediaries, Nexteco Energy Capital, and Steadfast Holdings LLC [Finding #6777].

Buskirk's organizational footprint is extensive. Rockbridge operates with a ~$75M budget and 150-200 members paying $100K-$1M in annual dues, steering eight organizations including two super PACs, four 501(c)(4)s, and a donor-advised 501(c)(3) [Finding #6742]. His Turnout for America super PAC raised $45.67M in the 2024 cycle [Finding #6741]. 1789 Capital has grown to over $3B in total AUM across 11 registered fund entities [Finding #6776] [Finding #6779].

Corporate filings show no record of Buskirk as an officer in most of his associated entities. American Greatness Inc. lists Ryan and Julie Gibson as officers; 1789 Foundation (which operates Citizen AG election litigation) lists the Yoder family and law partners. The only entity where Buskirk appears as a named officer is the Center for American Greatness 501(c)(3), where he is listed as President with $128,125 in compensation [Finding #6783]. Cross-referencing the filings, the recurring use of third-party officers across his entities suggests a consistent pattern of maintaining operational control while minimizing his own formal corporate footprint [Finding #6785]. He also co-owns the Executive Branch, a private Georgetown club with $500K founding membership fees, alongside Trump Jr., Malik, and the Witkoff brothers [Finding #6743].

sections.title: Career and Organizational Network
sections.content:
Buskirk was born on a US military base in Germany and raised in Scottsdale, Arizona. He graduated from Claremont McKenna College with a BA in Political Science and Government, followed by a Publius Fellowship at the Claremont Institute (1990 cohort, alongside Jeremy Fand, Agnes Howard, and Julie Ponzi) and an Earhart Foundation fellowship [Finding #6764]. His early career was in his father's insurance businesses in Scottsdale before founding JAS Intermediaries Ltd, Inc. (insurance/reinsurance intermediary), followed by Diversified Risk Management Holdings, Nexteco Energy Capital, Crucible Energy Partners (renewable energy tax credit financing), Americas Cash Express (consumer lending), and Steadfast Holdings LLC (family investment vehicle) [Finding #6777] [Finding #6765].

Buskirk sold most of his business operations around 2015 and pivoted to political media, co-founding American Greatness in early 2016 with Seth Leibsohn [Finding #6766]. He serves as publisher and editor, while also co-hosting 'The Seth and Chris Show' on 960 KKNT AM in Phoenix [Finding #6766]. His publishing credentials include opinion writing for the New York Times, Washington Post, USA Today, and The Hill, along with regular appearances on PBS NewsHour, NPR, Fox News, and CNN [Finding #6766]. He has authored three books through Encounter Books: 'American Greatness' (2017, co-authored with Leibsohn), 'Trump vs The Leviathan' (2018), and 'America and the Art of the Possible' (2023, blurbed by JD Vance) [Finding #6766].

The Center for American Greatness Inc. (EIN 81-4984970) is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit based at 3107 E Camelback Rd, Phoenix AZ, with 2023 gross receipts of $1.845M and 2024 revenue of $1.7M (99.8% from contributions) [Finding #6783]. Buskirk serves as President and Director ($128,125 compensation in 2024) [Finding #6783]. Fellow directors include J. Eric E. Wise (Secretary/Director, King & Spalding restructuring partner) and Ned Ryun, who also serves as director of Better Tomorrow, the Rockbridge Network's voter mobilization arm — a board overlap linking the publishing organization to the political operation [Finding #6783] [Finding #6780].

sections.title: Rockbridge Network Operations
sections.content:
Buskirk co-founded the Rockbridge Network with JD Vance in 2019, growing it from informal dinners near Rockbridge, Ohio into a 150-200 member donor coordination network with an estimated $75M budget for the 2024 cycle [Finding #6742]. Donors include Peter Thiel, Rebekah Mercer, and Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss [Finding #6742]. Membership costs between $100K and $1M annually [Finding #6742]. Buskirk runs day-to-day operations while Vance, now Vice President, provides the political profile [Finding #6742].

Rockbridge steers eight organizations: four 501(c)(4)s, two super PACs, one donor-advised 501(c)(3), and the umbrella LLC [Finding #6742]. Buskirk directly leads at least three subsidiaries: Turnout for America (super PAC, $45.67M raised in 2024), Firebrand Action (501(c)(4), established 2022, media and journalism arm), and Faithful in Action (Wyoming-registered, 160K+ members, Christian voter mobilization) [Finding #6767]. He also advised Saving Arizona PAC ($31.8M raised, $15M from Thiel), which backed Blake Masters's 2022 Senate run [Finding #6767].

Buskirk's relationship with Thiel predates Rockbridge. Reporting describes Thiel as having financed Buskirk's early political activism through committees that paid consulting fees to Buskirk's company, and as having introduced Vance to Buskirk [Finding #6771]. Marc Andreessen and Emil Michael have appeared at Rockbridge events as speaker and attendee, respectively, and Palmer Luckey has also spoken at Rockbridge gatherings [Finding #6771]. Leonard Leo spoke at the April 2024 Palm Beach retreat, connecting the Rockbridge donor network to the Federalist Society's judicial personnel network [Finding #6742].

sections.title: 1789 Capital and the Colombier SPAC Series
sections.content:
1789 Capital was co-founded in October 2022 by Buskirk (Founder & CIO), Omeed Malik (Founder & President), and Rebekah Mercer [Finding #6744]. The firm emerged from discussions at a Rockbridge Mar-a-Lago meeting in 2022 [Finding #6744]. SEC filings reveal 11 distinct fund entities registered under 1789 Capital, all originally at 214 Brazilian Ave Ste 200-J, Palm Beach FL, recently moving to 375 S County Rd Ste 220 [Finding #6772].

The original February 2023 Form D disclosed $10M raised from a single investor against a $100M target, with Malik, Mercer, and Buskirk as three Managing Members of the GP [Finding #6776]. By December 2025, Fund I LP had grown to $270.5M across 71 investors, and Mercer had been removed from filings [Finding #6776]. Total AUM across all vehicles exceeds $3B as of early 2026: the Growth Equity Fund grew from $200M to $2B in 2025 alone (now closed to new investors) and holds positions in SpaceX, Anduril, xAI, Neuralink, Groq, Cerebras, Perplexity AI, Plaid, and Ramp [Finding #6779]. A $1B real estate fund with Frisbie Group targets South Florida luxury properties [Finding #6779]. Donald Trump Jr. became a partner in November 2024 [Finding #6779].

The Colombier SPAC franchise is a public-markets arm of the 1789 Capital ecosystem. Colombier I (2021) merged with PSQ Holdings/PublicSq [Finding #6775]. Colombier II (2023, $130M IPO) merged with GrabAGun (online firearms retailer) on July 14-15, 2025, creating GrabAGun Digital Holdings Inc (NYSE: PEW) with $179M+ gross proceeds and near-zero redemptions [Finding #6774]. The GrabAGun board includes Trump Jr. (Director, 11,433 RSUs), Blake Masters (Director), and Chris W. Cox [Finding #6774]. Buskirk served as independent Director and Audit Committee Chair; his Form 4 discloses 17,250 Class A shares directly, plus 500,000 shares and 1,250,000 warrants indirectly via Anabasis VI LLC and 1789 Capital Fund I LP [Finding #6773]. Colombier III completed a $299M IPO on February 4-5, 2026, with a target still to be announced [Finding #6775]. Combined, the three SPACs have raised approximately $600M+ in public markets [Finding #6775].

sections.title: Political Infrastructure
sections.content:
Turnout for America (C00883520) raised $45.67M in the 2024 cycle [Finding #6741]. Top donors include Diane Hendricks ($11M), Kelcy Warren/Energy Transfer ($7.5M+), D. Andrew Beal ($2M), Howard Lutnick ($1.98M), Jeff Sprecher ($1M), Roger Penske ($1M), and Luke Nosek of the PayPal Mafia ($500K) [Finding #6741]. The PAC spent $4.66M on Patriot Grassroots for canvassing, $750K to America 21 PAC, $645K to Primo Communications, $562K to Timoleon LLC, $501K to Telperion LLC, $400K to Forward Strategies, and smaller amounts to Grigsby Applegate, Pulse Associates, American Majority Action, Crowned Eagle Consulting, and American Encore [Finding #6741].

America 21 PAC (C00804690), registered February 2022, is linked to Buskirk through shared operational infrastructure [Finding #6745]. He donated $30,500 personally [Finding #6748]. The PAC received $800K from Saving Arizona PAC (the Thiel-funded Blake Masters vehicle), $750K from Turnout for America, and $87.6K from Michigan Strong [Finding #6745]. FEC disbursement records show it uses an identical vendor network: Telperion LLC, Timoleon LLC, Pulse Associates, Crosby Ottenhoff, Holtzman Vogel PLLC, Howard Sckolnik CPA, and Chain Bridge Bank [Finding #6746]. America 21's largest single disbursement was $750K to MAGA KY, an anti-Thomas Massie PAC run by Republican strategists Fabrizio and LaCivita [Finding #6745]. Paul Singer donated $1M in November 2025 [Finding #6745].

Both PACs bank at Chain Bridge Bank (McLean, VA), founded by former Senator Peter Fitzgerald [Finding #6747]. Known as "the bank of the Republican Party," it has served every GOP presidential campaign since McCain 2008 and the RNC [Finding #6747]. Chain Bridge makes monthly interest deposits to both PACs: $28-39K per month to TFA and $1.9-4.5K per month to America 21 [Finding #6747]. The bank completed its IPO in October 2024, raising $41M [Finding #6747].

Faithful in Action (Wyoming-registered, 2023) is a church mobilization organization with 160K+ members, led by Buskirk as President, and Firebrand Action (Virginia, 2022) handles journalism for the Rockbridge network [Finding #6767].

sections.title: Proxy Officer Pattern
sections.content:
Buskirk is publicly identified as publisher, CIO, president, or founder of multiple entities, yet he is absent from nearly all corporate filings. Cross-referencing the filings, this absence runs through at least two distinct officer clusters [Finding #6785].

American Greatness Inc (EIN 45-2338676) was incorporated in Florida on May 5, 2011 — five years before the blog launched in 2016 [Finding #6782]. Its officers are Ryan C Gibson (President and registered agent), Julie C Gibson (Secretary/Treasurer), and Bonnie McQuiston (VP), all at 14 Alligator Cove, Santa Rosa Beach FL 32459, and the same three individuals operate SJ Consulting LLC (formed 2006) from the same residential address [Finding #6782]. Buskirk appears on none of the corporate records despite being publicly identified as publisher since launch [Finding #6782].

1789 Foundation Inc. (EIN 88-3099118), the legal entity behind Citizen AG election litigation, was founded in May 2022 in Florida [Finding #6781]. Its officers are Eric Scharfenberger (President), Gabrielle Yoder (Secretary), and Nicole Cristine Pearson (Treasurer) [Finding #6781]. Mike Yoder founded Citizen AG; Gabrielle Yoder is his wife [Finding #6781]. The entity operates from a Northwest Registered Agent address at 7901 4th St N Ste 300, St. Petersburg FL [Finding #6781]. Buskirk does not appear on any filing [Finding #6781]. The law firm Yoder Dreher Pearson LLP connects all three officers [Finding #6781].

The sole entity where Buskirk appears as a named officer is the Center for American Greatness Inc., the 501(c)(3) research arm [Finding #6783]. Taken together, the filings suggest a recurring practice — the Gibson household for the media entity, the Yoder legal cluster for the litigation entity — that lets Buskirk retain operational control while keeping his own name off the corporate record [Finding #6785].

sections.title: Executive Branch Private Club
sections.content:
Buskirk is co-owner of the Executive Branch, a private club in Georgetown, DC, alongside Donald Trump Jr., Omeed Malik, Alex Witkoff, and Zachary Witkoff (sons of Steve Witkoff, Trump's Middle East envoy) [Finding #6743]. Founding membership costs $500K [Finding #6743]. Founding members include David Sacks, Chamath Palihapitiya, the Winklevoss twins, and Jeff Miller [Finding #6743].

Documented attendees include Secretary of State Rubio, Attorney General Pam Bondi, DNI Gabbard, FCC Chair Carr, FTC Chair Ferguson, SEC Chair Atkins, Dan Bongino, and Mehmet Oz [Finding #6743]. Reporting describes the club as designed to give business executives private access to Trump advisors and Cabinet members [Finding #6743].

The Palm Beach address cluster further connects Buskirk and Malik: 214 Brazilian Ave Ste 200-J houses 1789 Capital, Colombier Sponsor II LLC, Knights Court LLC (Malik as manager), and Pecora1718 LLC (formed February 2025, purpose unknown) [Finding #6778]. The shared Palm Beach address is consistent with an operational relationship between Buskirk and Malik spanning investment, SPACs, and political access [Finding #6778].

sections.title: FEC Donation History
sections.content:
FEC records show Buskirk's personal political contributions across multiple cycles [Finding #6748]. In the 2021-2022 cycle, with employer listed as 'CAG' (Center for American Greatness): $30,500 to America 21 PAC, $5,800 to Ohioans for JD (Vance super PAC), $2,900 to JD Vance for Senate, $2,900 to Working for Ohio, and $5,800 to WinRed [Finding #6748].

In the 2023-2024 cycle, with employer listed as 'self-employed' or 'CAG' from Paradise Valley, AZ: $110K to Trump 47 Committee, $106.7K to RNC, $5.8K to Blake Masters for Congress, $10K to Vance Victory, $5K to JD Vance for Senate, $5.6K to Never Surrender Inc, and $5.3K to WinRed [Finding #6740]. Across both cycles, his personal giving exceeds $290K, directed to Trump committees, Vance-linked vehicles, and Masters [Finding #6767].

Records show the early timing of Buskirk's Vance donations: the September 2021 donation to Ohioans for JD predates the Senate primary [Finding #6748]. His son, Christopher Buskirk Jr. (listed as student, Paradise Valley AZ), donated $500 to Brandon Gill for Texas in January 2024 [Finding #6748].

sections.title: 1789 Foundation Election Litigation
sections.content:
1789 Foundation Inc., operating as Citizen AG, filed three coordinated voter roll challenge cases within 72 hours of each other in late October 2024 — a pre-election litigation strategy targeting swing states [Finding #6787].

In Arizona, 1789 Foundation v. Fontes (2:24-cv-02987) was filed October 28, 2024 [Finding #6787]. A temporary restraining order was denied on November 1, but the court ordered voter roll records released [Finding #6787]. The case was voluntarily dismissed on May 8, 2025 [Finding #6787]. The lead attorney was Alexander Kolodin (AZ state representative, District 3), who had been disciplined by the Arizona Bar in December 2023 — receiving 18 months probation — for filing frivolous cases, including serving as local counsel for Sidney Powell's 'Kraken' lawsuit (Bowyer v. Ducey, 2:20-cv-02321) [Finding #6784]. Kolodin is now running for Arizona Secretary of State in the 2026 Republican primary [Finding #6784].

In Pennsylvania, 1789 Foundation v. Schmidt (3:24-cv-01865) was filed October 30 [Finding #6787]. A TRO and preliminary injunction were denied October 29 [Finding #6787]. Plaintiffs failed to file an amended complaint, and the case was finally dismissed on June 10, 2025 [Finding #6787].

In Wisconsin, 1789 Foundation v. ERIC (3:24-cv-00755) challenged ERIC's use of driver records under the DPPA [Finding #6787]. WisDOT and CEIR were dismissed as parties by January 2025; the case against ERIC and David Becker remained ongoing as of November 2025 with discovery stayed pending motions to dismiss [Finding #6787].

Nicole Cristine Pearson, who serves as 1789 Foundation's treasurer, simultaneously acted as litigation counsel in the Arizona case — concentrating fiduciary and legal control in the same individual [Finding #6786]. Her firm Yoder Dreher Pearson LLP, co-founded with Mike Yoder and Rachel Dreher, handled Citizen AG litigation across all three jurisdictions [Finding #6786].

curation.system_role: Buskirk demonstrates how a single operator can build an integrated political-financial platform spanning media, donor coordination, venture capital, public-market vehicles, election litigation, voter mobilization, and executive access while remaining absent from nearly all corporate filings through systematic use of proxy officers.
open_questions: Buskirk's name is absent from nearly all corporate filings across his organizational network. What is the full scope of this proxy officer arrangement — are the Gibson cluster (American Greatness Inc.) and the Yoder cluster (1789 Foundation) the only two, or do additional proxy officer groups exist for Rockbridge subsidiaries, Firebrand Action, or Faithful in Action? [Finding #6785]

1789 Capital's original Form D listed Rebekah Mercer as one of three Managing Members of the GP. By December 2025, she had been removed from filings. What triggered Mercer's removal — was it a genuine divestiture, or a cosmetic change to reduce public visibility of her involvement? [Finding #6776]

Turnout for America and America 21 PAC share an identical vendor network (Telperion LLC, Timoleon LLC, Pulse Associates, Crosby Ottenhoff, Holtzman Vogel, Howard Sckolnik CPA, Chain Bridge Bank). Who are the beneficial owners of Telperion LLC and Timoleon LLC — both Delaware entities — and do any of these vendors have direct financial relationships with Buskirk beyond their PAC service contracts? [Finding #6746]

The Executive Branch club charges $500K founding memberships and hosts sitting Cabinet members and agency heads. Are any of the club's founding members or attendees also investors in 1789 Capital funds or Colombier SPACs, creating a potential overlap between executive-branch access and investment relationships? [Finding #6743]

Anabasis VI LLC is disclosed on Buskirk's Form 4 as holding 100K shares and 250K warrants in the GrabAGun/Colombier II merger. This entity does not appear in Florida Sunbiz or Delaware records under that name. What is the full corporate structure of the Anabasis entity series, and does it function as Buskirk's personal investment holding vehicle? [Finding #6773]
